items.title: Melaka sanctuary's green anaconda gives birth to 10 after 7 months without food
items.summary: AYER KEROH: A 2.74m-long green anaconda named Diana has given birth to 10 offspring at the Melaka Butterfly and Reptile Sanctuary after going nearly seven months without food. The sanctuary's managing director, Gerard Wong, said Diana gave birth on Monday after a gestation period of about 190 days. He said the birth marked a milestone in wildlife conservation, as the offspring represent the second generation of green anacondas bred at the sanctuary.

items.title: 'We will not return': Imran Khan supporters march for his release
items.summary: Punching the air and roaring in Unison, ecstatic crowds joined a growing demonstration on Wednesday in support of Pakistan's jailed former prime minister Imran Khan, an opposition show of force that authorities had sought to avert. Supporters of Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party began their so-called "long march" on Sunday, demanding his release and airing anti-government sentiment fuelled by harsh economic conditions. "I joined this procession for one reason: Imran Khan's release.

items.title: Mercy Malaysia rolls out nationwide haze emergency response
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mercy Malaysia is rolling out its Haze Emergency Response nationwide to supply medical aid and health guidance to vulnerable groups as air quality worsens across several states. In a statement today, the humanitarian organisation said the initiative builds on its ongoing efforts in Sarawak, where it has supported public health advocacy, community awareness and assistance for those affected by haze. "Haze is currently affecting several parts of Peninsular Malaysia, including Johor, Negri Sembilan, Melaka, Selangor and Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Song Swee Guan's legacy and SUPP's unfinished comeback
items.summary: Sarawak bade farewell to a towering political legend in the person of Datuk Song Swee Guan this week. Song had served four terms as a state assemblyman representing Padungan in Kuching, now an opposition stronghold. When Kuching was elevated to city status in 1988, Song became its founding mayor.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Police to strengthen operational capabilities, combat digital crime
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police will optimise the allocations under the 2027 Budget to strengthen operational readiness, enhance enforcement capabilities and address increasingly complex digital crime threats. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the force was committed to ensuring that every allocation was utilised efficiently and with integrity to improve the effectiveness of police service delivery. "Police also welcome the RM1.1 billion allocation to enhance the operational capabilities of enforcement agencies in addressing increasingly complex security challenges," he said in a statement.

items.title: NST Leader: The haze crisis needs more than promises
items.summary: The sudden school closures as pollution readings inch towards highly "unhealthy" levels are more than just a health emergency. It is natural for Malaysians to blame Indonesia, where the forest fires—often deliberately set—originate. Malaysia has rightly sought Indonesia's cooperation.

items.title: Malaysians in Saudi Arabia advised to avoid high-risk areas amid security tensions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Embassy in Riyadh has advised Malaysians in Saudi Arabia to stay calm and follow official safety directives following recent security developments in the Gulf country. "The embassy remains in contact with the Saudi Arabian authorities and will communicate any significant developments requiring the attention of Malaysians through official channels," the statement said. Malaysians requiring emergency consular assistance can contact the Malaysian Embassy in Riyadh via its hotline at +966 56 300 6319 (emergencies only) or email mwriyadh@kln.gov.my.

items.title: Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize for career defending international law
items.summary: OSLO: The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded Friday to South Africa's Navi Pillay, the judge who headed the Rwanda genocide tribunal and presided over a UN commission which accused Israel of genocide in Gaza – a move angrily denounced by Israel. The 85-year-old, who is currently a judge on the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in a case in which Myanmar also stands accused of genocide, has spent her career defending international law. Pillay has been "instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide are prosecuted," said Jorgen Watne Frydnes, the chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee in Oslo.

items.title: Prosecutors drop bribery charge in Philippine VP impeachment trial
items.summary: MANILA: Prosecutors said Friday they are dropping a bribery charge against Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte, who still faces three other charges at her ongoing impeachment trial that could lead to her removal from office. The 48-year-old is also charged with misuse of state funds, unexplained wealth, and an alleged assassination threat against one-time ally President Ferdinand Marcos. Prosecutors have already presented evidence and witnesses in support of the assassination and misuse of funds charges.

items.title: Thai queen flies Gripen fighter jet solo for the first time
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thailand's Queen Suthida has flown a Gripen fighter jet solo for the first time, the royal household revealed Friday, watched on by her husband King Maha Vajiralongkorn, himself a keen pilot. The outing followed weeks of simulator training at the base and about 10 hours in a two-seat Gripen, media reports said. Thailand already operates a squadron of Gripen C/D fighters made by Sweden's Saab, and last year signed a deal for three Gripen E jets and one Gripen F worth around US$556 million, with deliveries due by 2030.

items.title: Civil servants ready to implement 2027 Budget swiftly - Shamsul Azri
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar is confident civil servants are ready to ensure government policies, including 2027 Budget, are implemented swiftly and effectively. Shamsul Azri also expressed his appreciation to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, for tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today. The budget also provides for Special Financial Assistance of RM1,500 for civil servants and RM750 for government retirees.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Don't leave contract pharmacists behind, govt told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's move to offer permanent positions to more than 9,000 contract doctors under the 2027 Budget has prompted calls for similar clarity on the future of contract pharmacists, who continue to face employment uncertainty. The Malaysian Pharmacists Society (MPS) said contract pharmacists should not be overlooked in efforts to address longstanding job insecurity in the public healthcare sector. Its president, Professor Amrahi Buang, welcomed the government's announcement but said pharmacists who had served for years in public hospitals, health clinics and other Health Ministry facilities also deserved a clear pathway to permanent employment.

items.title: Thai court dismisses detention challenge by Chinese reporter
items.summary: BANGKOK: A Thai court on Friday dismissed a challenge by a Chinese investigative journalist over his prolonged detention in Bangkok, a day after authorities began proceedings to extradite him to China, his lawyer said. Bai Zhaodong, who is recognised by the United Nations as a refugee, left China in 2023 and arrived the following year in Thailand. China's foreign ministry said in July that Bai was suspected of extortion and bribery, and an extradition request had been submitted to Thailand.

items.title: Egyptian president El-Sisi arrives for 2-day state visit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi arrived at the Bunga Raya Complex at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) about 6.20pm today to begin a 2-day state visit to Malaysia. He was received by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. The visit is El-Sisi's first to Malaysia since he became Egypt's president in June 2014.

items.title: Plantations Ministry to study cooperation with Indonesia to prevent Kalimantan fires
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Plantation and Commodities Ministry will study a proposal to strengthen cooperation with Indonesia to prevent and control forest and land fires, including through the Council of Palm Oil Producing Countries (CPOPC). The ministry said the cooperation could include information sharing and efforts to prevent and control fires in Kalimantan, following reports linking Malaysian plantation companies to forest and land fires in Indonesia. "Through the Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB), the ministry held an engagement session with six Malaysian companies on Sept 10 to obtain information on the fire situation and the preventive and control measures in place in their respective operating areas," it said in a statement.

items.title: Two women burnt to death in Myvi-lorry collision in Yong Peng
items.summary: The victims were identified as Perodua Myvi driver Siti Nur Batrisya Mohd Khalid and her front-seat passenger, Siti Nurmaisarah Abd Jalil. Ayer Hitam Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Mohd Shamin Mohamed Salikin said the station received an emergency call at 4.21pm, and a team arrived at the scene four minutes later. Shamin said both victims were burnt beyond recognition.

items.title: 2027 Budget: MCMC steps up connectivity, digital safety and AI initiatives
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget, tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in the Dewan Rakyat today, outlines several government initiatives to strengthen the country's digital infrastructure through programmes implemented by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC). Anwar said MCMC will step up efforts to improve internet connectivity, strengthen digital safety and accelerate artificial intelligence (AI) adoption under the 2027 Budget, backed by a RM5 billion allocation for the National Digital Network Plan (Jendela), which includes plans to extend 4G coverage to all Orang Asli villages next year. Beyond digital safety, the government is looking to accelerate AI adoption, develop local expertise and strengthen the country's digital capabilities.

items.title: Singapore prepares to distribute N95 masks as haze nears 'very unhealthy' levels
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore said on Friday it was "ready to roll out" a haze pollution action plan that included the distribution of masks, as air quality dipped towards "very unhealthy" levels. "Based on the current situation it is possible" that air quality levels "may enter the very unhealthy range," Singapore's National Environmental Agency said in a statement. It said the government has set aside haze-rated masks and if pollution levels dipped into very unhealthy levels, "grassroots organisations will start distributing N95 masks to eligible Singaporeans."

items.title: RM935mil tourism allocation offers opportunities for Sabah, says Jafry
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah is looking to strengthen its tourism sector through improved international connectivity, destination promotion and conservation following the tabling of the 2027 Budget. State Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the RM935 million allocated for tourism and culture nationwide would create opportunities for Sabah to promote its destinations, develop tourism products and preserve its cultural heritage ahead of Visit Sabah 2027. "Sabah welcomes the emphasis placed on the tourism sector, particularly efforts to improve facilities, strengthen promotion and expand international flight connectivity.

items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. items.title: 2027 Budget: Here are the key announcements [WATCH]
items.summary: The expansionary fiscal policy mobilises RM510 billion in overall national resources, up from RM470 billion previously. The breakdown is as follows: * RM376.8 billion in federal operating expenditure; * RM83 billion in federal development expenditure; * RM25 billion in investments by government-linked investment companies (GLICs); * RM11 billion in public-private investments; and * RM14.2 billion in investments by federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance Incorporated companies. Minimum wage increased to RM2,000 The minimum wage will rise from RM1,700 to RM2,000, effective June 2027.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 9, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Budget eases tax burden The 2027 Budget raises personal tax relief to RM12,000 and cuts tax rates for middle-income earners. Mother disputes classification Zara Qairina Mahathir's mother told the Coroner's Court she disagreed with classifying her daughter's death as a Sudden Death Report. Haze disrupts routines Worsening haze has disrupted daily life and forced parents to make last-minute childcare arrangements following school closures.

items.title: 2027 Budget drives economic growth through efficient capital formation and mobilisation – SC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget provides strong momentum for the Securities Commission's (SC) efforts to drive economic growth through efficient capital formation and mobilisation, the capital market regulator said. In a statement, the SC said that the key measures will accelerate the priorities of its Capital Market Masterplan 2026-2030 (CMP), enhancing the vibrancy, inclusivity, sustainability and regional competitiveness of Malaysia's capital market. Its chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi said that the targeted measures and capital market instruments provide the first step in delivering the SC's masterplan in growing the market as well as deepening inclusivity.

items.title: Indonesia takes legal action against individuals, firms over forest fires
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesia is taking legal action against individuals and corporations over forest and land fires, with 198 suspects identified in 247 police reports, says the Indonesian Embassy in Malaysia. In a statement today, the embassy said a further 97 police reports involved corporations. The Environment Ministry had identified 57 business entities across eight provinces, with 33,514.01ha of burned land within concession areas.

items.title: NUTP: Ensure RM69bil education budget reaches schools that need it most
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Spending under the Education Ministry's nearly RM69 billion allocation in the 2027 Budget must be prioritised according to actual needs, particularly school safety and well-being, says the National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP). Its secretary-general Fouzi Singon said the allocation, the largest among ministries, must be managed transparently and distributed efficiently to deliver meaningful improvements in schools. Fouzi said the allocation should also strengthen school security, rather than focus solely on physical infrastructure upgrades.

items.title: Guardian: Tax relief to ease family healthcare costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Guardian Malaysia says the 2027 Budget's higher healthcare tax relief will help ease medical costs for households and make essential healthcare more affordable. Guardian Malaysia welcomed the measures to ease healthcare costs, including an increase in individual tax relief to RM12,000 from RM9,000. She said families facing financial pressure might postpone smaller healthcare needs to prioritise immediate living expenses.

items.title: Civil servants praise 2027 Budget's bid to tackle cost-of-living issues
items.summary: KUCHING: The special financial assistance of RM1,500 for civil servants and RM750 for government retirees and veterans is expected to help ease the cost-of-living burden, particularly in meeting daily necessities, children's education and family commitments, while also stimulating domestic spending. "This highlights the need for financial support to help households adjust their spending amid rising living costs. Meanwhile, retired serviceman Azhar Ishak, 56, said the increase in Special Financial Assistance (BKK) to RM750 in 2027 was a positive development that would help ease the burden on retirees.

items.title: RM19.1bil Higher Education allocation must address lecturers' welfare, workload
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Higher Education Ministry's RM19.1 billion allocation under 2027 Budget must translate into improvements in lecturers' welfare and working conditions amid growing academic and administrative demands. She said greater attention must be given to lecturers' workload, career development and well-being, rather than focusing solely on university rankings and research achievements. Fauzilah, who is also a principal research fellow at Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin's Islamic Social Finance Research Centre, said lecturers' responsibilities had expanded well beyond teaching.

items.title: Civil servants to get RM1,500 aid, pensioners RM750 under Budget 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A total of 1.3 million civil servants in Grade Utama B and below, including those on contract appointments, will receive RM1,500 in special financial assistance under Budget 2027. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the finance minister, announced the assistance when tabling the Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today. More than one million government pensioners, including pensionable and non-pensionable veterans, will also receive RM750 each.

items.title: 2027 Budget: RM2k minimum wage falls short of workers' needs – MTUC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC) has described the RM2,000 minimum wage as insufficient, saying it falls short of the RM3,100 it had sought and the RM3,400 living wage paid to employees of government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs). MTUC secretary-general Kamarul Baharin Mansor said the wage gap had created a three-tier system among lower-income workers, with differences between minimum wage earners, micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) workers, and those receiving a living wage. He said exempting MSMEs from the minimum wage requirement would create confusion and discrimination, with workers performing similar jobs paid differently depending on their employers' status.

items.title: TNB's RM15 bil grid investment to support power reliability, industrial growth -- Solarvest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) RM15 billion investment in the national grid announced in Budget 2027 today addresses a critical priority and need for the infrastructure to support reliable power and industrial expansion, said Solarvest Holdings Bhd. Solarvest chief executive officer Datuk Davis Chong Chun Shiong said the company would work with TNB to advance smart grids, digital energy management and utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) to meet rising corporate demand under the accelerated Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS). Meanwhile, Malaysia Petroleum Resources Corporation (MPRC) president and chief executive officer Mohd Yazid Ja'afar said Budget 2027 would help Malaysian oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) companies strengthen sustainability, develop skills in new energy sectors and expand into global markets.

items.title: Rehda backs Budget 2027 housing measures but calls for more action on rising costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda) has welcomed measures in Budget 2027 to support homeownership, while urging the government to do more to address rising development costs and housing affordability. Its president, Datuk Zaini Yusoff, said in a statement that the expanded stamp duty exemptions for first-time homebuyers would help reduce the upfront cost of buying a home. The association also welcomed stamp duty exemptions for rehabilitating abandoned housing projects, saying they could help revive projects and provide relief to affected purchasers.

items.title: PLUS to close Bangi Toll Plaza road shoulder for widening works until June 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — PLUS Malaysia Berhad (PLUS) will temporarily close the road shoulder after the exit lane of the Bangi Toll Plaza towards Bandar Baru Bangi from today until June 28 next year to facilitate road widening works. In a statement today, PLUS said the works were scheduled to take approximately eight months as part of the company’s ongoing efforts to improve highway facilities and enhance users’ comfort. Users are also advised to plan their journeys and obtain the latest traffic updates through the PLUS app, the company’s official social media platforms, including its X account @plustrafik, and electronic message signs (VMS) at selected locations.

items.title: Budget 2027 draws positive response from ministers over focus on living costs, wages and public services
items.summary: Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the measures reflected public feedback gathered through nationwide engagement sessions, particularly concerns over rising living costs and the need for better wages. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister, earlier tabled Budget 2027, which places greater emphasis on boosting household disposable income and supporting middle-income earners alongside continued economic reforms. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi speaks during a press conference at Parliament in Kuala Lumpur on October 9, 2026.

items.title: E-Commerce Bill to protect small traders, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government will table an E-Commerce Bill at the next parliamentary sitting to strengthen accountability among online platforms and sellers, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said. He said the government was urgently examining legislative and enforcement measures to protect micro, small and medium enterprises from unfair competition and ensure goods purchased by consumers were safe. The fifth Madani Budget, themed “Malaysia Madani: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi”, is the second budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan.

items.title: Budget 2027: Home, Defence Ministries each allocated RM22b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Home Ministry and Defence Ministry have each been allocated RM22 billion under Budget 2027, tabled in the Dewan Rakyat today. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said RM7.1 billion of the total allocation would be channelled to procure and maintain assets for the armed forces, police, and uniformed agencies under the Home Ministry. Anwar also said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had blocked more than 5.7 billion scam-related calls and SMS messages.

items.title: Malaysia’s approved investments rise 11.7pc to RM218.5b in first half of 2026, says PM
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Malaysia’s approved investments rose 11.7 per cent to RM218.5 billion in the first half of 2026, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. “For example, Sime Darby Property, the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) and the Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) have established the RM1.25 billion New Economy Venture Fund to develop data centres and logistics assets in Elmina, Selangor,” he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today. Meanwhile, he said Khazanah Nasional Bhd and the Retirement Fund (KWAP) had invested RM1.2 billion to help local semiconductor companies move up the value chain.

items.title: Budget 2027: RM2.62b aid for paddy farmers, incentives for fishermen, smallholders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government is allocating RM2.62 billion in aid to paddy farmers under Budget 2027, covering various subsidies and incentives to increase rice production and safeguard their welfare. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the assistance would enable paddy farmers to receive benefits of about RM4,300 per hectare of paddy field, including subsidies for seeds, fertiliser, pesticides, ploughing costs and paddy prices. “To rehabilitate and rejuvenate paddy fields, RM20 million will be provided to supply foliar fertiliser for more than 10,000 hectares of paddy fields.

items.title: Budget 2027: RM8b for TVET, 30,000 new job opportunities via BAKAT Madani
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was also targeting 30,000 new job opportunities through the BAKAT Madani initiative next year, including through the participation of private companies. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said that under the overall skills development initiative, HRD Corp, with an allocation of RM3 billion, would offer three million skills training opportunities, including for continuing professional development among professionals. He said the Skills Development Fund Corporation (PTPK) had allocated RM500 million to finance trainees enrolled in skills training programmes at public and private skills training institutes registered with the corporation.

items.title: PM Anwar: Registration to open next week for affordable smart city Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil
items.summary: Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said nearly RM1 billion has also been allocated for projects under the People-Friendly Homes (Rumah Mesra Rakyat) and People's Residency Programme (Program Residensi Rakyat). “Four new housing projects will be implemented in Kulai, Johor; Nilai, Negeri Sembilan; Paya Rumput, Melaka; and Lembah Pertang, Terengganu,” he said. Anwar also announced that the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) will provide housing financing guarantees of up to RM20 billion.

items.title: Budget 2027: Health minister vows to complete 9,000 contract-to-permanent doctor transitions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Health Ministry (MoH) will complete the process of appointing 9,000 contract doctors to permanent positions throughout 2027, effectively ending the interim contract doctor system, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said. When tabling the budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that more than 9,000 contract doctors would be offered permanent positions next year, while doctors who complete their housemanship in the future would be offered permanent posts as medical officers. Anwar also said that since 2023, the Madani Government had appointed more than 15,000 contract doctors to permanent positions, including 4,000 this year.

items.title: Ringgit gains against US dollar as Budget 2027 underscores fiscal discipline
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The ringgit closed higher against the US dollar today, supported by the government’s commitment to fiscal consolidation under Budget 2027, an analyst said. At 6pm, the ringgit climbed to 4.0830/0875 against the greenback from yesterday’s close of 4.0890/0940. “The expected narrowing of the fiscal deficit suggests that the government remains committed to fiscal discipline, which can effectively help bolster confidence among traders and investors towards the ringgit,” he told Bernama today.

items.title: ‘Today is for the rakyat, tomorrow is for the wife’: Syed Saddiq’s Budget 2027 reply amuses social media
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Muar Member of Parliament Syed Saddiq Abdul Rahman left local social media users amused following his response to a post on Threads. “Today is for the rakyat, tomorrow is for the wife. “From fiancée, to future wife to now just wife, so cute,” commented user nadhrahy_.

items.title: Sabah, with RM18.6b in allocations, hails 2027 budget as alleviating burden for all Malaysians
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 9 — Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor described the National 2027 Budget as a comprehensive budget that alleviates the people's financial burden and reflects the strength of the country's economy. In Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s proposed budget, Sabah continues to be the biggest recipient of federal allocations with RM18.6 billion for next year, an increase of 6.25 per cent compared to RM17.6 billion for this year. In addition, Anwar said road projects in Sabah and Sarawak would continue with an allocation of RM3.3 billion under the 2027 Budget.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng calls Budget 2027 Anwar’s ‘most reform-minded’ yet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today described Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s fifth Madani Budget as the “most reform-minded” budget yet. Lim, who is also Bagan MP, said expanding the social safety net to gig workers, persons with disabilities and senior citizens, providing more inclusive funding allocations and adjusting personal income tax rates to address past injustices were steps in the right direction. Still, Lim said more needed to be done, particularly by allocating 10 per cent of total Bumiputera allocations to non-Bumiputera communities without reducing existing Bumiputera funding.

items.title: Budget 2027: Medical groups hail end to contract doctor system, enhanced public-private synergy but seek more on retention
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Healthcare stakeholders had mixed responses to the national health allocations announced in Budget 2027, with the Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) applauding the move to end the contract doctor system while highlighting critical gaps in workforce retention The Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM), meanwhile, welcomed measures to boost public-private cooperation. We commend the Government for taking this important step towards providing greater job security and career certainty for our young doctors,” he said. MMA also said more emphasis should be placed on strengthening primary healthcare to tackle NCDs.

items.title: Four injured after lorry crashes into 11 vehicles in Shah Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 9 — Four people were injured in an accident involving a lorry and 11 other vehicles at Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, Alam Budiman here today. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department was informed of the crash at about 4.30pm and immediately dispatched personnel to the scene. “The accident left a man and a woman with serious head injuries, while two other male victims sustained minor injuries,” he said in a statement.

items.title: MEF welcomes RM2,000 minimum wage, says MSME exemption gives smaller firms breathing room
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) today welcomed the federal government’s decision to raise the national minimum wage to RM2,000 while exempting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales of less than RM50 million. MEF senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said a balanced approach was essential to ensure efforts to improve workers’ welfare did not inadvertently undermine business viability, discourage hiring or put existing jobs at risk. Explaining further, Syed Hussain said a responsible wage policy focuses not only on the extent of wage increases but also on ensuring businesses can sustain those wages, protect existing jobs and continue creating new employment opportunities.

items.title: Haze: 36 areas record unhealthy API readings, Pasir Gudang highest at 190
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A total of 36 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5.45pm today, with Pasir Gudang in Johor recording the highest reading at 190. In Negeri Sembilan, three areas recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Seremban (189), Nilai (183) and Port Dickson (174), while in Melaka, the affected areas were Bukit Rambai (187), Bandaraya Melaka (183) and Alor Gajah (181). A total of 32 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while no areas recorded good readings.

items.title: Budget 2027: Government-owned Entities Bill to be drafted next year, RM1.1b for enforcement agencies’ operations
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the Finance Minister, made the announcement while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today. “With the Government Procurement Act coming to force starting 2027, the government will improve transparency and publish project details, including the contractors and contract value,” Anwar said. Anwar also said revenue generated from loan repayments, including from education and business loans, disbursed to federal statutory bodies must only be used for the approved purposes and target groups.

items.title: Budget 2027: Bumiputera contractor procurement nearly doubles to RM7.5b, GLICs to invest RM2b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government is set to increase the procurement allocation for Bumiputera contractors in the G1 to G4 grades to RM7.5 billion under Budget 2027, an increase from RM4 billion this year. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this follows recent concerns raised by Bumiputera contractors and companies. “This also provides opportunities for Bumiputera construction, engineering, and maintenance companies.

items.title: Budget 2027: Form Six students to receive RM2,500 allowance, early school aid increases to RM200 per pupil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Form Six students will receive a RM2,500 cost-of-living allowance each next year, matching the rate given to matriculation students, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. Speaking during the tabling of Budget 2027 in Parliament, Anwar said the assistance would benefit 90,000 Form Six students nationwide. Anwar also announced that the government would increase Bantuan Awal Persekolahan (BAP), or early schooling assistance, from RM150 to RM200 per pupil next year.

items.title: Budget 2027: Govt rolls out six initiatives to attract global firms, skilled talent
items.summary: Tabling Budget 2027, Anwar outlined six initiatives to improve Malaysia’s business environment and competitiveness, amid renewed investor confidence in recent years. Among other measures, Anwar said the existing Global Services Hub (GSH) incentive will be further improved starting January 2027. “New companies under the GSH incentive will enjoy a special five per cent tax rate on income from GSH activities.

items.title: Budget 2027: Government earmarks RM60m for Matrade, RM1b to boost MSME exports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 - The federal government will allocate RM60 million to the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) to help build local companies’ capacity to enter and diversify their overseas markets, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. In his Budget 2027 speech, Anwar said Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Berhad (BPMB) will also prepare RM1 billion to support local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to explore the export market. He said JOM Malaysia will also have RM10 million to bring rural products and high-value services to digital platforms and overseas markets.

items.title: Budget 2027: Government halts public university disciplinary proceedings relating to free speech
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government has halted disciplinary proceedings at public universities relating to freedom of speech, expression of views, public criticism and peaceful assembly with immediate effect. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Higher Education Ministry was preparing a comprehensive legal framework to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), covering university autonomy, academic freedom and student rights. “With immediate effect, all disciplinary proceedings at public universities relating to freedom of speech, expression of views, public criticism and peaceful assembly have been halted,” Anwar told the Parliament today during the tabling of the Budget 2027.

items.title: Anwar: Voluntary medical insurance MediAsas to kick off in 2027, EPF Akaun Sejahtera can pay premiums
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — MediAsas, a voluntary medical insurance and takaful plan, will be launched nationwide at affordable prices in January 2027, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. While tabling Budget 2027 at Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said MediAsas would help keep hospital bills under control and more predictable according to diagnosis type. Anwar also said Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contributors under 55 years old can also tap into their Akaun Sejahtera to pay for MediAsas premiums.

items.title: Budget 2027: Duty‑free shopping limit in Langkawi and Labuan raised to RM10,000
items.summary: However, Anwar said visitors and tourists must stay for at least 48 hours to enjoy the higher duty-free shopping limit. “More locally made products from Langkawi will also be exempted from import duties to support local entrepreneurs,” he said. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said this when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Budget 2027: Higher Education Ministry gets RM19.1bil, RM800mil for university facilities upgrades
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Higher Education Ministry will receive RM19.1 billion under Budget 2027. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this will include RM800 million to upgrade university facilities and replace ageing equipment. A slight increase from the Budget 2026 allocation of 18.6 billion, the Budget 2027 allocation follows a broader expansion of the ministry’s responsibilities, with Form Six and matriculation students set to come under its purview from 2027, bringing pre-university education within the higher education system.

items.title: Budget 2027: Entertainment duty exemption for local film, theatre tickets in Federal Territories, creative sector gets RM130m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Tickets for local films and theatre performances in the Federal Territories will be fully exempt from entertainment duty starting in 2027, as part of the government’s efforts to support the local creative industry. The government will also strengthen the local animation ecosystem to develop 20 new intellectual properties (IPs) and commercialise Malaysian characters globally. The government also called on state administrations to introduce similar entertainment duty exemptions to support local creative practitioners.

items.title: Budget 2027: e-ART to be main urban public transport solution in Johor Bahru ahead of RTS Link
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The federal government today said the Elevated Autonomous Rapid Transit (e-ART) system would be the main solution for easing traffic congestion in Johor Bahru. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would also add bus routes, increase bus and KTM Komuter service frequency, and provide Grab shuttle services in high-demand areas ahead of the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link opening next year. “Traffic congestion in Johor Bahru must be addressed immediately.
